path_ledger._arc_rule: FORMAL, second edition (operator's review 2026-08-08 caught a circularity in the first: if dependence had to be PROVEN for the arc to exist, an unproven nerve could hide behind 'no dependence established, so no arc yet'). EXISTENCE and STATUS are separate questions. A CANDIDATE ARC exists wherever a value actually crosses a phase or module boundary and enters a consumer — no proof of effect required; entering the queue is what makes the effect investigable. STATUS then grades the proof: UNPROVEN — dependence not yet shown; PARTIAL — part of the causal chain proven (e.g. delivery yes, effect mock-blind: the prompt_to_model family is PARTIAL by construction); PROVEN — dependence + semantics + protection shown; DEAD — absence of causal effect proven. An arc ends at the last consumer provable without a live model; hops into a live model form their own PARTIAL arcs. Granularity notes may group physical sites; they never delete a candidate. CLAUSE SHARPENED 2026-08-08 after the operator made me defend turn_context_read: a granularity note may group ONLY the physical sites of the SAME value -> SAME consumer-contract pair (several call sites delivering one routed model to one planner contract, say). Different VALUES or different CONSUMERS are different candidate arcs however tidy it would be to group them — the rule needed no weakening, it had been violated: one record had held prompt blocks, a suppression flag and a durable stats write under a single CERTIFIED verdict, and one of those consumers had never been tested. goal -> retrieval (C15) is the standing example of the other half of the rule: a candidate arc held as UNPROVEN precisely because its dependence is not yet shown.

Statuses from path_statuses; UNPROVEN never becomes an assumption; a call edge is never a proven signal flow. A cluster is closed only when its report (SCOPE -> EXECUTION PATH -> SIGNALS/STATE -> OWNERSHIP -> FAILURE SEMANTICS -> TEST EVIDENCE -> MUTATION EVIDENCE -> VERDICT -> NEXT EDGE) exists and its critical contracts have proven bites. knowability._question: The operator's question, asked before any classification: after launch and with no operator input, can this contour choose useful work? Three sub-questions, three answers from code and from the live workspace.
knowability.where_the_contour_gets_work: EXACTLY ONE call site in the repository puts a task into the queue: core/scheduler.py:217, inside SchedulerStore.tick(), and it converts a DUE SCHEDULE into a task. Schedules have exactly one producer, SchedulerStore.add (core/scheduler.py:142), reached only from _handle_schedule_add (app/task_scheduler_cli.py:292) — the operator's :schedule-add. Enumerated, not assumed: no enqueue exists in api/server.py (the file holds no queue reference at all), none in the campaign path, none in self-build, and none in agent_tick.py itself. So every unit of autonomous work traces back to an operator command.
knowability.what_the_contour_holds_when_it_starts: Measured on the live workspace 2026-08-14, not read off comments: data/runtime_schedules.jsonl is 0 rows, and TaskQueueStore.pending() against the real store returns 0 tasks (13 rows present, none pending — pending() honours run_after and status). Step 1 of run_tick therefore enqueues nothing and step 2 claims nothing. build_agent sits inside the `else` of `if not pending_tasks`, so with an empty queue the agent is never built, AutonomousRuntime is never constructed, and the loop never runs. The tick logs no_pending_tasks and performs only the approval-inbox check. This is the shipped configuration, not a broken one.
knowability.was_the_choice_of_work_knowable: YES, mechanically. select_best_next_action (core/best_next_action.py:99) is pure — it takes structured signals and returns exactly one BestNextAction, always, including 'just observe'. Its consumers are cli/commands_approval.py:143 (an operator command) and core/campaign_io.py:72 (the --campaign mode). It is NOT reached from agent_tick.py or run_tick. So the deciding value is computable at precisely the point where the tick concludes it has nothing to do, and no arc carries it there. Its own docstring forbids the other half: 'pure and advisory ... never executes the action'.
knowability.what_this_does_not_establish: That any of it is a defect. The contour was SPECIFIED as scheduler-driven: agent_tick.py's header states the six steps of a tick and step 1 is 'load scheduler store -> find schedules that are due'. Choosing work is not among the six. Making the tick a consumer of best_next_action would be a contract change and is the operator's call. No defect claimed, no runtime change in this unit.

carry_forward._rule: Closed units are not re-audited by default and not inherited blindly either. Independently: a later discovery of a new consumer, state space, observer or contradiction REOPENS a closed unit. PROVEN is a result relative to the search that was performed, never a claim that undiscovered consumers cannot exist.

replan_decision_action.preconditions_proven: All three states shown reachable from decide() before any equivalence claim: continue (budget available), abort_no_retry (per-type budget exhausted 2/2), abort_exhausted (global cap 3/3). Probed directly, not inferred from tests.
